question: Does training a warning detector with incident-informed synthetic anomalies, derived from verified attack and failure literature, improve detection of recorded real attacks (HAI 22.04) and recorded real production incidents (SMD) over a normal-only world-model residual detector at the same false-alarm budget, and is any gain specific to the incident knowledge rather than to synthetic anomalies in general?
evidence_class: External real-telemetry check. HAI 22.04: real boiler, turbine and water-treatment hardware with a HIL power-generation stage and attacks staged by the dataset authors. SMD: real production servers with incidents labelled by domain experts from incident reports. No runtime authority, actuator or deployment is involved.

hai-22.04.final: test1-4 with the per-second Attack label
hai-22.04.sensors_and_actions: Actions are the setpoint, demand, schedule, controller-output and operator-command tags listed in scripts/real_telemetry_data.py (HAI_ACTIONS); all other varying tags are sensors; tags constant over train1-6 are dropped. Decided from training files only.

partitions.world_model_selection: fit train1-4, validate train5-6 (probe run before this registration and retained)
partitions.detector_training: injected and clean windows from train4-5
partitions.calibration_and_selection: train6 (clean for thresholds; injected copies for selection)

smd.development: train files of 28 machines (normal period; may contain unlabelled anomalies)

partitions.world_model_selection: per machine: fit first 80% of train, validate last 20% (probe run before this registration and retained)
partitions.detector_training: per machine: injected and clean windows from 50-80% of train, pooled across machines

data.final_access_rule: Test files and labels are read only through real_telemetry_data.hai_test / smd_test, which append to target/real-telemetry/final_access.jsonl. Before the selection freeze the ledger must not exist. The final evaluation runs once.

injection.generic_control: generic_noise: Gaussian corruption of 1-4 random variables with the same duration and magnitude distributions
injection.targeting: Actions uniformly at random; sensors coupled to an action by absolute correlation of first differences; correlated sensor groups by absolute correlation of first differences between sensors; all computed on normal fitting data. HAI attack targets are never used.
injection.held_out_use: Held-out families are never used to train or select any detector; they are a development diagnostic of generalization to unseen mechanisms.

world_model.selection_rule: Lowest mean of validation H1 and H5 MAE (robust-scaled units) among the non-persistence candidates.

detectors.D0_persistence_residual: Top-3 mean of |Z_t - Z_{t-1}| / sigma, sigma from the world-model fitting data.
detectors.DR_range_gradient: Bound and gradient check in the style of Wolsing et al. (ESORICS 2022): max over variables of the exceedance beyond the normal fitting range and beyond the maximum normal step, in robust units.
detectors.D1_world_model_residual: Normal-only: top-3 mean of |H1 residual| / sigma1 plus top-3 mean of |H5 residual| / sigma5, sigmas from the detector-training partition's clean residuals.
detectors.D2_incident_informed: LightGBM classifier on per-step residual, delta and action features, trained on clean windows plus windows with one development-family injection each.
detectors.D3_generic_control: Same classifier, features, windows and budget as D2, with generic_noise injections only.
detectors.selection_rule: For each detector independently, choose the smoothing window that maximizes event recall on injected development-family validation windows at the calibrated threshold. No other detector setting is tuned.

calibration.alarm_episodes: Steps with score above threshold are merged into episodes when separated by at most the merge gap (HAI 60 s; SMD 10 min).

budget.hai: 2 false alarm episodes per day of clean calibration data
budget.smd: 1 false alarm episode per machine-day of calibration data

calibration.threshold: The smallest threshold whose clean-calibration false-episode rate is within the budget (per machine for SMD).

endpoints.primary: Event recall on the final data: a labelled attack or incident run is detected if any alarm step falls inside it.
endpoints.false_alarms: False alarm episodes per day on the final data (episodes overlapping no labelled run).
secondary: point-level AUC-PR and AUC-ROC (no point adjustment)
median detection delay of detected events
world-model H1/H5 MAE on final normal periods versus persistence

gates.primary_hypothesis: For each dataset, D2 versus D1: relative miss reduction at least 20% and the lower bound of the 97.5% paired event-bootstrap interval (10,000 resamples, Bonferroni across two datasets) above zero, and D2's final false-alarm rate at most twice its calibration budget.
gates.primary_success_rule: Both datasets pass the primary hypothesis.
gates.specificity: Secondary, per dataset: D2 versus D3 relative miss reduction with a 97.5% paired event-bootstrap interval excluding zero.
gates.reporting: All detectors, both datasets, failures and inconclusive results are reported. No claim of runtime authority, deployment safety or real-incident prevention follows from any outcome.

limitations_registered_in_advance: HAI attacks are staged by the dataset authors on a testbed; SMD labels have documented quality issues (Wu and Keogh, TKDE 2021).
Injected anomalies modify recorded telemetry; process responses to injected commands are generic first-order responses, not plant physics.
The author viewed the HAI technical manual's attack table before registration; targeting was made random to limit leakage.
SMD has no command variables, so its world models are autonomous forecasters.
